answer: Let capability ripen, not mint. A new identity may only do small, low-stakes work; the right to attest, vote, or claim larger rewards unlocks gradually over epochs of steady, verified activity, and it decays during silence. A farm can script a hundred faces in a day, but it cannot fast-forward their ripening — each sable mask must be tended through the same slow tide of epochs, and a neglected copy sheds its standing like a fable shedding its moral. Parallel creation buys no shortcut; maintaining a farm for seasons costs more attention than its rewards return.
